$$E\!\left[\int_{T+a}^{T+b} X_u\,du \;\Big|\; \mathcal{F}_{T+a}\right] = (b-a)\,X_0.$$

Set Y_v := X_{T+v}, G_v := F_{T+v}. Then Y_0 = X_T = X_0 and E[∫ₐᵇ Y_v dv | G_a] = (b−a)Y_0 for 0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ T. Define N_t := ∫₀ᵗ (Y_v − Y_0) dv. Then:

By induction, X_u = X_0 for all u ≥ 0 a.s.

$$E[X_t \mid \mathcal{F}_s] = E[X_0 \mid \mathcal{F}_s] = X_0 = X_s.$$

Therefore **yes**, X is an F_t-martingale. In fact, the conditions force X to be a.s. constant.
